authorization.execution_results: No MVP implementation, endpoint design, benchmark execution or human validation performed in this step.
authorization.step_3_approval: Explicit user approval received 2026-10-21; Step 3 only; all entities/data synthetic; local direct stakeholder validation pending.

all_synthetic_requirement.source: User instruction: All data synthetic including all entities.
all_synthetic_requirement.rule: Invent fixtures from scratch in a clearly marked demo namespace. Do not import actual records and rename people. Use invented organizations and non-deliverable contact addresses.
all_synthetic_requirement.verification: NADRA and PMDC outcomes are local simulated fixtures only. State changes are controlled in the test environment and labelled simulated.
all_synthetic_requirement.enforcement: Authentication, authorization, persistence, provenance checking and negative-case blocking must actually execute in the MVP; synthetic data does not mean simulated security behaviour.
all_synthetic_requirement.network: The MVP demonstration must function with outbound service access disabled, apart from its own local application traffic. No live NADRA/PMDC, email, SMS, appointment or hospital/laboratory calls.
all_synthetic_requirement.research_context: Public literature and real-provider documentation are cited only as background evidence and are not demonstration entities/data.

research.question: Does a reproducible molecular-report handoff protocol enforce correct access and preserve correction lineage across changes in patient consent, appointment state and separately evidenced professional registration/hospital affiliation, without blocking valid workflows?
research.candidate_contribution: A Pakistan-informed conformance profile and reproducible synthetic state-transition benchmark for version-specific patient-authorized report release.
research.novelty_limits: Established RBAC/ABAC, consent, CNIC-supported enrolment, credential verification, version history and multi-entity exchange are not claimed as new. Originality and a Pakistan commercial gap are unconfirmed.
research.close_prior_art: SMDEE (2025) already describes multi-entity privacy-rule checking and patient preferences. KP hospital standards already describe credential verification and hospital incumbency documentation.

comparison_arms.name: Properly configured conventional reference
comparison_arms.requirements: Use established role/attribute access controls, explicit per-report-version consent, appointment/time restrictions, independently represented registration and affiliation, current-state checks and ordinary report versioning/audit capabilities. Configure every feature the reference supports rather than artificially disabling it.
comparison_arms.independence: Use a separately specified policy table/evaluator and disclose whether the reference is a constructed prototype or an actual incumbent. A shared-stack reference is an internal comparison, not an independent commercial security audit.

comparison_arms.name: Proposed integrated handoff workflow
comparison_arms.requirements: Same agreed authorization semantics, data, available evidence and infrastructure, with explicit transition handling, issuer-bound provenance and decision explanations.
comparison_arms.interpretation: The system is not assumed superior. Equal correctness means no security advantage was demonstrated.

comparison_arms.name: Optional isolated ablations
comparison_arms.requirements: Individually remove version binding, independent affiliation checking or current-state revalidation in the isolated synthetic evaluation harness.
comparison_arms.interpretation: These intentionally incomplete variants are not the primary baseline and do not represent Pakistani products.

fairness: Same fixture states, inputs, expected outcomes, request order, workload and documented hardware.
Do not give the proposed system credential/source evidence that the reference does not receive.
Freeze policy, cases and expected outcomes before implementation/evaluation; version any later amendments and retain failures.
Report configuration effort and limitations for each arm; a locally built reference cannot establish the capabilities of a real competitor.
Use a domain-reviewed expected-outcome table independent of production code; do not use the MVP's own decisions as ground truth.
Review missing reference capabilities explicitly rather than treating an unimplemented feature as proof of insecurity.
research.analysis: Report raw numerators/denominators separately for authorization, submission admission and provenance/state assertions, plus paired case differences between arms. Synthetic purposive cases are not population samples; do not claim population risk, clinical effectiveness or statistical superiority from repeated scripted requests.
research.decision_rule: If both arms satisfy all requirements, describe conformance and measured operational differences. If a claimed advantage disappears with a normal reference configuration, withdraw that superiority claim. If the proposed system fails any mandatory release gate, fix and re-evaluate before demonstrating readiness.
not_measured_here: Actual NADRA or PMDC identity-verification accuracy
National demand, willingness to pay or clinical outcomes

physician_release_requires: Correct linkage of the requested report to the enrolled synthetic CNIC patient
Accepted issuer-approved report version and intact content
Explicit active patient grant for this physician, appointment, hospital context, purpose and exact report version
Professional registration evidence independently valid within its declared interval
Hospital affiliation evidence independently valid for the same context within its declared interval
policy_semantics.other_roles: Patient access is restricted to the patient's own linked records. A lab sees/submits only its authorized work. Hospital profile management gives no clinical-record access. Technical roles do not gain unrestricted report access through public role flags.
policy_semantics.time: Use authoritative server/test-clock time and half-open validity intervals [start, validUntil). Test immediately before, exactly at and immediately after every boundary. The production freshness policy is not determined by this synthetic benchmark.
policy_semantics.credential_snapshots: Registration and affiliation are separate dated attestations. Unknown, pending, stale, revoked or expired evidence does not satisfy the corresponding release condition. No live real-world validity guarantee is implied.
policy_semantics.version: A grant for version 1 cannot fetch version 2. An authorized old version may remain accessible only as explicitly historical/superseded. The current corrected version requires a fresh matching grant.
policy_semantics.submission: A held report is not visible as an accepted clinical report. Replay has no additional clinical effect, and no version is destructively overwritten.
policy_semantics.revocation_order: Let t_commit be the durable local commit of a consent/appointment/credential change. Every new request whose authorization decision is ordered after t_commit must use the changed state. Already delivered or already authorized in-flight data cannot be recalled; new requests from the same session remain subject to rechecking.
policy_semantics.evidence_outage: Clinical access is denied when required identity/credential evidence is unavailable or a required access audit cannot be durably recorded. Public physician-profile browsing may continue without exposing clinical data.
policy_semantics.privacy: Retain only necessary identity evidence. Keep full CNIC test values out of routine URLs, logs, patient-facing audit summaries and public physician profiles. Do not display credentials or verification documents publicly.
policy_semantics.audit_meaning: An authorization/access event records the server's decision and delivery outcome where known; it does not prove that a human read or understood a report.

threat_model.assessment_type: Prospective application threat model, not a repository scan or validated vulnerability report.
assets: Audit trail and patient disclosure summaries
trust_boundaries: Client input to authenticated server operations
Lab submission to accepted patient record
Hospital profile attestation to independent professional-registration evidence
Consent/credential state to every report/file release
Application storage to protected signing/integrity evidence
Raw administrative audit to a restricted patient-readable access summary
assumptions: The local OS/runtime and protected key/checkpoint material remain trusted.
Authorized institutional issuers may still make clinical mistakes; source authentication cannot certify analytical truth.
Adversaries may possess their own legitimate role accounts and may reuse an earlier valid physician session.
Only the isolated synthetic MVP and evaluation harness are tested; external services/products are not attack targets.

threats.actor: Outsider or patient using another person's identifier
threats.failure: CNIC guessing, enumeration or recovery is used to obtain a different patient's account or history.
threats.required_response: Separate identity proof, authentication and authorization; protect recovery and generic error handling; no CNIC-only login/reset.

threats.actor: Authenticated laboratory or accidental entry error
threats.failure: A genuine report is attached to the wrong patient/order/specimen.
threats.required_response: Check against independently enrolled patient and expected order/specimen context; quarantine inconsistencies.

threats.failure: Direct IDs, downloads, alternate routes or role fields bypass object/function authorization.
threats.required_response: Apply server-side role and per-record checks to every clinical path; never trust posted roles or verification flags.

threats.actor: Registered physician or hospital profile submitter
threats.failure: Valid PMDC registration is treated as hospital affiliation, affiliation as registration, or listing as record permission.
threats.required_response: Check independent evidence and validity for both credential states; neither grants access without explicit patient consent.

threats.failure: Old session, grant or cached file link continues to disclose records after an applicable state change.
threats.required_response: Re-evaluate the committed local state for each new request, including file paths; appointment and identity context cannot drift.

threats.failure: An altered report or metadata with a recomputed hash is accepted as laboratory approved.
threats.required_response: Bind authorized issuer evidence to metadata and actual content; a bare hash alone is insufficient.

threats.failure: Replay or rollback makes an obsolete report current; concurrent corrections destroy lineage.
threats.required_response: Persist unique submission identity and predecessor checks; reject/quarantine conflicts and preserve original versions.

threats.actor: Concurrent valid request and state mutation
threats.failure: A check/use race releases data using permission already invalid at the request's agreed ordering point.
threats.required_response: Define atomic ordering between permission decisions and committed state changes; capture ordering evidence.

threats.failure: Audit/history can be edited or truncated without evidence, or sensitive data is returned with no durable access event.
threats.required_response: Restrict modification and bind integrity checks to protected evidence/checkpoints; fail closed for clinical release if the required audit write fails.

threats.failure: CNIC, credentials, clinical metadata or report bodies leak through lists, errors, logs, notifications or shared browser cache.
threats.required_response: Minimize fields, mask identifiers, isolate sessions and protect clinical responses from inappropriate caching; test each relevant response surface.

threats.failure: Malicious uploads, stored HTML, injection, oversized requests or request floods cause unauthorized actions, crashes or unbounded processing.
threats.required_response: Validate input, escape presentation, limit resource use, protect state-changing requests and enforce documented abuse controls.

threats.actor: Session thief or user on a shared device
threats.failure: Logout/revoked sessions remain usable or authorization is broader than the compromised account's current grant.
threats.required_response: Enforce server-side session revocation and role/grant limits; no claim that the MVP detects all theft of an otherwise valid session.

residual_limits: A fully compromised application host plus signing keys/checkpoints is outside this MVP assurance boundary.
A deliberately dishonest trusted lab/hospital issuer can assert false facts; tests check digital authorization and consistency, not truth.
A valid session can be stolen and used within its current rights before detection; no universal phishing resistance claim.
Screenshots or copies previously obtained by an authorized person cannot be revoked.
No high-volume DDoS resilience, national interoperability deployment, compliance certification or clinical safety claim.

families.name: CNIC identity, authentication and recovery
families.focus: A formatted or known CNIC never authenticates a user or proves identity; unverified enrolment, expired session and invalid additional verification are rejected.

families.name: CNIC to order and specimen matching
families.focus: Bind independently enrolled patient, lab patient ID, order and specimen. Hold mismatches without an automatic patient merge.

families.name: Separate registration and affiliation
families.focus: Registration-only, affiliation-only, client-asserted verification and unauthorized profile approval do not satisfy both checks.

families.name: Appointment and explicit consent
families.focus: Booking alone grants nothing. Consent is bound to the named physician, appointment, hospital context, purpose, report version and time interval.

families.name: Record ownership and role boundaries
families.focus: Test another patient, physician, laboratory, hospital role and direct object/file identifiers. A role or unpredictable ID is not sufficient authorization.

families.name: Report correction and version scope
families.focus: Authorized correction creates a linked successor; original stays historical; permission for one version does not broaden silently.

families.name: Issuer evidence and content integrity
families.focus: Reject unapproved issuer, changed metadata or file bytes, missing clinical/specimen context and recomputed bare hashes without valid issuer evidence.

families.name: Replay, rollback and conflicting submissions
families.focus: Duplicate messages have no additional effect; stale versions cannot become current; conflicting corrections cannot silently overwrite one another.

families.name: Audit, provenance and privacy
families.focus: Record expected events and version-specific origins; deny ordinary-role audit alteration and avoid full CNIC/secret disclosure.

families.name: Persistence and transaction failures
families.focus: Committed records survive restart. Interrupted writes do not create half-grants, orphan successors or unlogged clinical releases.

families.name: Untrusted input and abuse
families.focus: Reject disallowed types, excessive sizes and invalid structures; safely handle injection/HTML/path inputs and unauthorized cross-origin writes; enforce documented throttling.

families.name: Credential freshness and local revocation
families.focus: Exercise before/at/after expiry, unknown or stale verification, consent withdrawal, cancelled appointment, invalidated registration and revoked affiliation with an already logged-in physician.

benchmark.development_and_reserved: Per family: 7 development cases (3 valid, 4 adverse) and 3 reserved variants (1 valid, 2 adverse), giving 84 development and 36 reserved cases. Reserved does not mean independently blinded unless a separate reviewer actually creates/controls them.
benchmark.prerequisites: Materialize and freeze concrete fixtures and expected outcomes before building the implementation under later authorized steps. The present step defines the protocol only.
benchmark.endpoint_coverage: Every later clinical read/file route and privileged mutation route must map to at least one positive and one unauthorized case. Add cases if route coverage requires more than 120; never delete failures to fit the budget.

transitions: Hospital affiliation revocation versus report read
Recorded professional-registration invalidation versus report read
Two corrections competing for the same predecessor
concurrency.oracle: No read decision ordered after a committed invalidation may release data. At most one conflicting successor becomes current unless both are explicitly serialized as valid successive corrections; no silent lost update.

benchmark.repetitions: Run each primary arm from the same clean initial fixture state. Use fresh-process reruns for persistence/order-sensitive cases; do not count repeated requests as independent subjects.
boundary_and_failure_coverage: Restart after committed permission and correction
Changed report bytes with recomputed unkeyed hash
benchmark.expected_results_status: Not run; no performance, accuracy or security results yet.

acceptance.name: Complete protocol conformance
acceptance.target: All 120 planned unique cases pass their predeclared outcomes, including all 48 valid workflows and all 72 adverse/failure cases; any added route-coverage cases must also pass.
acceptance.denominator: Unique cases in the frozen manifest

acceptance.name: Unauthorized clinical release
acceptance.target: 0 report bodies, file bytes or prohibited clinical fields released for expected-deny read requests.
acceptance.denominator: All expected-deny clinical requests, separately reported for each family and route

acceptance.name: Valid workflow rejection
acceptance.target: 0 unexpected denials or holds in predeclared healthy valid cases. Legitimate amendments and renewed sharing must complete.
acceptance.denominator: All expected-valid workflow actions; report exact count

acceptance.name: Submission admission and integrity
acceptance.target: 0 mismatched, unapproved, tampered or rollback submissions admitted as accepted clinical reports; every valid submission/correction remains traceable.
acceptance.denominator: Expected-invalid and expected-valid submission actions, reported separately

acceptance.name: Concurrent ordering
acceptance.target: 0 ordering or lost-update violations in 500 coordinated traces. The first new request after a committed invalidation is denied without requiring logout.
acceptance.denominator: 100 traces for each of the five transitions

acceptance.name: Provenance and version retention
acceptance.target: 100% of accepted report versions contain their required issuer, approver, source/report/order/specimen IDs, relevant test context, timestamps, integrity evidence and status. All amendments retain predecessor, reason and authorizer; originals are retrievable as historical records.
acceptance.denominator: Accepted report versions and amendments, not all test requests

acceptance.name: Audit completeness and integrity
acceptance.target: 100% of manifest-required security events are durably represented with actor, action, relevant object/version, time, outcome, decision basis and correlation ID. Ordinary-role edits/deletions fail; injected alteration/truncation is detected against protected integrity evidence within the stated trust boundary.
acceptance.denominator: Expected logical security events from the case manifest; multiple low-level entries may map to one logical event

acceptance.name: Privacy and all-synthetic isolation
acceptance.target: 0 real entity/record fixtures, 0 live verification/messaging calls, 0 full test-CNIC or authentication-secret leaks outside explicitly permitted restricted identity input/storage. Simulated verification labels remain visible.
acceptance.denominator: Fixture inventory, responses/logs/exports and captured runtime network destinations

acceptance.name: Recovery
acceptance.target: After a controlled restart, 100% of committed reports, grants, credential states, version links and audit events remain consistent; interrupted operations produce no half-applied clinical release or correction.
acceptance.denominator: Committed state assertions and interrupted transaction cases

acceptance.name: Local performance
acceptance.target: Proposed engineering budget: p95 server authorization/metadata response <= 1000 ms over 1000 mixed requests (500 permitted, 500 denied), at concurrency 10, after a separate warm-up, on the documented demo laptop. Return no protected body on denied responses; report timeouts/errors rather than excluding them.
acceptance.denominator: All 1000 benchmark requests, including errors; file transfer, login and human verification durations measured separately

acceptance.name: Fair comparative reporting
acceptance.target: Report R and M per-case correctness, error counts, p50/p95/max latency, setup/configuration time, constraints and unresolved issues under the same workload. No mandatory superiority claim.
acceptance.denominator: Identical frozen cases and workload for both primary arms

acceptance.name: Usability and local adoption evidence
acceptance.target: Keep status pending. Later real reviewers may use only synthetic records, but scripted role agents cannot establish patient comprehension, clinician acceptance, institutional feasibility or willingness to pay.
acceptance.denominator: No new participants in this step

deliverable_gate: A working MVP must demonstrate real access enforcement, persisted synthetic data and all mandatory engineering gates. A successful synthetic demo is not a clinically deployed or stakeholder-validated product.
